## Ruling recorded — A, with the translations authored by AI: all four locales land together with the form-child enumeration (director seat, decision batch #120 item 3, 2026-09-12)

Maintainer, verbatim (live PM chat, 2026-09-12T04:2xZ), to decision batch #120 presented as `1A·2A·3D·4B·5C′`: 「17508 A AI负责翻译就行。其他同意」.

The seat had recommended D (en + zh-CN now, ja / es left to fall back until a translator is named) on the reading that product copy is a human's. The maintainer's word settles the resourcing question the card was filed to ask: **AI authors the translated copy** — 「AI负责翻译就行」. ⇒ A as the card recommended, with the dev seat (an AI) writing the 604 catalog leaves.

### What is ruled
1. One coherent landing: the `*.form.ts` child enumeration for the 13 carriers / 83 properties PLUS the `en` / `zh-CN` / `ja-JP` / `es-ES` catalogs, pinned the way `dashboard-header-children.test.ts` pins the #17227 leaves — including its last test: a translated leaf is ⛔ never a copy of the `en` source.
2. The translations are authored by the dispatched dev in the same PR; quality bar: a native-reading column head, consistent with the existing terms in each locale's catalog (reuse the words the catalog already uses for the same concept; ⛔ no new term for a concept the catalog already names).
3. `priority:p3`: nothing is broken today (English reaches every locale through the fallback chain); the value is the finished product surface.

### State
`needs-user-decision` → `pm:queue`; `domain:spec` kept; `priority:p3` added (the card carried none).

## ⭐ The direction is RULED, including the part the card was filed to ask — ⛔ this card carries no options

This card was filed as a decision card and it has been answered. Ruling at comment `5643444868`, **decision batch #120 item 3**, maintainer verbatim: 「**17508 A AI负责翻译就行。其他同意**」.

⭐ **Read that carefully, because it settles the resourcing question, not just the option letter.** The filing seat recommended D (English plus `zh-CN` now, `ja` / `es` left to fall back until a translator is named) on the reading that product copy is a human's to write. The maintainer overruled that: **the dispatched dev — an AI — authors the translated copy.** ⇒ you write all four locales. ⛔ Do not stop and ask who translates; that IS the answered question.

Quoted from the ruling so you work from it:

> 1. One coherent landing: the `*.form.ts` child enumeration for the 13 carriers / 83 properties PLUS the `en` / `zh-CN` / `ja-JP` / `es-ES` catalogs, pinned the way `dashboard-header-children.test.ts` pins the #17227 leaves — including its last test: a translated leaf is ⛔ never a copy of the `en` source.
> 2. The translations are authored by the dispatched dev in the same PR; quality bar: a native-reading column head, consistent with the existing terms in each locale's catalog (reuse the words the catalog already uses for the same concept; ⛔ no new term for a concept the catalog already names).
> 3. `priority:p3`: nothing is broken today (English reaches every locale through the fallback chain); the value is the finished product surface.

⛔ Option B is refused by the ruling and by an existing pin: landing `en`-only leaves is the half-state `dashboard-header-children.test.ts` exists to refuse, because its last test asserts each translated leaf is **not** a copy of the `en` source. ⇒ an `en`-echo catalog either reds that pin or normalises English strings masquerading as translations. ⛔ Neither is acceptable and ⛔ neither is a way to make the round smaller.

## The figures on the card are a 2026-09-10 reading — ⭐ re-take them

The card states 604 catalog leaves across four locales, 348 of them belonging to the 87 properties titled today, across 14 carriers, measured at `origin/main` `76ddab772f`. **Ten days and several sibling landings have passed.** #17505, #17506 and #17502 have all closed since, and each of them moved this surface.

⇒ **re-derive the population on your own base**, through the platform's own predicate the way #17232's round did (`z.toJSONSchema` over `getMetadataTypeSchema`), ⛔ not by regexing source. Report the numbers you measure and say plainly if they differ from 604 / 348 / 87 / 14. A changed count is a **good** finding, ⛔ not a problem with the card.

⚠️ Two specific traps this exact surface has already sprung on this lane, both worth your attention:
- A repeater whose item schema is a **union** must have every arm treated as a separate candidate; merging the arms answered `columns` as an integer once and silently dropped a carrier.
- Reading a property node **as Studio does** rather than dereferencing `$ref` first is what caught a title bug that would otherwise have shipped as two false ledger entries.

## Fenced out of this round

- ⛔ The `retiredKey()` tombstones are **#17502's** subject and ⛔ must not be titled.
- ⛔ `view.columns` / `view.tabs` / `view.sort` titling is **#17507's**, a sibling card that is open and unclaimed. ⛔ Do not title them here even if your census surfaces them; say in your report that you saw them and left them.
- ⛔ The objectui repository is READ, never edited.

## On `Clause-②: no` above

Enumerating a repeater's children in a `*.form.ts` and adding catalog leaves adds no key to a published payload and moves no accept set — the same author input parses identically before and after. That is the declaration.

⚠️ **But the review is owed anyway**, and you should know why so the label does not surprise you: the enqueue gate has two independent limbs, and the PATH limb hits on `packages/spec/src/**` whatever the declaration says — this order's own `--tier` run prints the SUSPECT line. ⇒ when your draft PR exists, this seat hangs `needs:contract-review` on **both** the card and the PR and routes the verdict to an isolated at-tier reviewer. ⛔ You do nothing about that label.

⭐ **If your diff turns out to WIDEN anything** — a new key, a form input for something not authorable, a describe that changes what parses — **say so and stop.** This seat corrects the declaration with the prescribed `Clause-②-correction:` form, ⛔ never a second `Claim:`.

## Acceptance

- The re-derived population, with instrument, radius, a **lit control** (a term known present, > 0) and a **dark control** (a fabricated term, 0), exit codes captured **before any pipe**.
- All four locales authored, with the ruling's quality bar met: reuse each catalog's existing word for a concept it already names; ⛔ no new term for an already-named concept. Say in the report how you checked that for each locale.
- The pin extended in `dashboard-header-children.test.ts`'s shape, **including** the last test — a translated leaf is never a copy of its `en` source.
- Every gate from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived from the tree you are on, exit codes to a file, reconciled with `--ran`.
- `bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh --status` re-read before your first heavy run; exit **99** is NOT MEASURED, ⛔ not red.
- A changeset graded from what actually moved, with the reason stated. `packages/spec` is published (`private` unset, `17.4.0`, `files[]` ships `src/**/*.zod.ts`); read the manifests of every package you touch rather than assuming.
- PR opened as a **draft**, first line `Fixes #17508`, with a line-initial `Clause-②:` line carrying whatever arm your measurement supports.

## Charter increments for this round

1. ⛔ Do not leave a second claim comment — this one is the identity. Verify the newest claim on this card names your branch; if not, stop and report.
2. ⛔ Every GitHub payload, title included, is built from a file by a script — never an inline double-quoted shell string.
3. ⛔ Capture every exit code BEFORE any pipe; `grep -c` counts LINES, not occurrences.
4. ⭐ Every reading states its base sha and the clock it was read at. This order's readings were taken at 2026-09-20T11:00Z against `origin/main` = `e3b3cdd2df3`; if the base has moved when you start, re-take them.
5. ⭐ Report anything here you measure to be false rather than working around it. The figures in this order are ten days old and this seat expects at least one of them to have moved.

## Seat record — at-tier review PASS, base merged BEFORE the review, carriers cleared, enqueued

Written at 2026-09-20T13:19Z by `session_01LvwGppdonww4zGLWZo5rho` (`domain:spec` execution seat 1). Delivery: PR #19345, head `74dcce59635a0b7d0f1f5b487a0e8dc0bd806da1`.

### ① Review of record — PASS

Comment `5750013153` on the PR thread, an isolated at-tier contract review naming this head, taken in the reviewer's own detached worktree. Tier verified afterwards by counting the harness-stamped per-message `model` field in the reviewing round's transcript, ⛔ never the dispatch parameter: **150 at tier / 150 total / 0 off-tier**, dark control 0. Adopted verbatim; ⛔ not edited.

⭐ **It did the thing no gate can do.** The ruling put the translated copy in an AI's hands, so the one axis with no mechanical reader is whether the copy is any good. The review read **336 of 336** hand-authored leaves: 0 en-echoes, 153 reusing a rendering the catalog already had, 183 with no exact precedent, and **0 competing renderings** for a string already translated elsewhere — which is exactly the ruling's bar (「reuse the words the catalog already uses; ⛔ no new term for a concept the catalog already names」). Two weak spots are named rather than waved through: `ja` `app.areas.id` renders エリア ID while the same panel's repeater label is 領域, and `zh` `flow.edges.type` uses 连接类型 where 连线 is the sibling term. Neither blocks.

⭐ **And it proved the pin is not vacuous, by its own ablation** rather than by reading the test: it set one `zh-CN` leaf back to its `en` source (blob `5df9a8c` → `819e861`) and the eighth test — the 「a translated leaf is never a copy of the source」 one — failed by name on `zh-CN skill:triggerConditions.operator`; restore put the blob back and all 8 passed.

### ⭐⭐ The base had moved, and this time it was merged FIRST

The standing rule is 「当基座移动时,先并 main **再**派发 at-tier 复核」. On PR #19315, earlier in this same shift, this seat broke that rule by reading `pulls/{n}.base.sha` as the merge base — it is the base BRANCH's tip and says nothing about ancestry (filed as #19325). Here the same question was measured with the right instrument:

```
git merge-base origin/main HEAD   81e12e186f3  (4 commits behind main)
git merge-base --is-ancestor      NO
```

⇒ `origin/main` was merged into this PR at 2026-09-20T12:50:33Z through `PUT /pulls/19345/update-branch`, **before** the reviewer was dispatched, and the head moved `1cf7f2ae8ca` → `74dcce596` with main confirmed an ancestor afterwards.

⚠️ **The merge was only safe because it was measured first.** This diff carries four generated translation catalogs, and the `os-regen` driver DEFERS on routed both-sides paths — a deferred merge silently keeps ONE side while `git show --stat` never names the file. Overlap between the 4-commit delta and this PR's 16 files was measured **zero**, with the PR file list intersected against itself (16) as the instrument control. ⛔ Had there been overlap, `update-branch` would have been the wrong tool.

### ② Clause-② carriers

`check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 19345` exit **0**, recognising comment `5750013153` as the C6 record on this head and at tier. Both carriers then removed two seconds apart — card 2026-09-20T13:12:58Z, PR 2026-09-20T13:13:00Z.

`Clause-②: no` stands, and the reviewer re-derived it rather than adopting it: 16 files, 10 `*.form.ts`, **no `.zod.ts`**, `check-widening-tells --declaration no` reporting no tell. ⭐ It also found a derived side effect the round did not claim — **6 `[REMOVED]` tombstone columns that used to render are no longer offered** (5 on `dashboard:widgets`, 1 on `flow:nodes`). That narrows the rendered surface toward the accept set and widens nothing, so the declaration holds.

### ③ CI

The strip re-fired `Check Changeset` at 2026-09-20T13:13:04Z and it concluded `success`; `Lint & Repo Gates` concluded `success`. Re-read latest-per-name after that write: **35 checks, 0 not green**, plus the `Vercel` commit status. ⇒ ready 2026-09-20T13:18:51Z, auto-merge armed, `added_to_merge_queue` 2026-09-20T13:18:53Z.

### The card's own figures moved, as this seat's order predicted

604 leaves total is unchanged, but the **titled** share is now **504 / 126 / 18**, ⛔ not the card's 348 / 87 / 14 — #17505 paid `dashboard:widgets` (17) and `dashboard:globalFilters` (10), #17506 paid `field:options` and `object:fields.options` (6, one shared `SelectOptionSchema`). 87+27+12 = 126 and 14+4 = 18. The reviewer reproduced 21 carriers / 151 live row properties / 126 titled / 25 untitled exactly.

⭐ **One pre-existing shipped string MOVES, and it is a defect the enumeration exposed rather than caused.** `page.variables`' children were enumerated without labels, so the extractor emitted the humanised path `Source` and the overlay wrote it over the schema's authored `Written By` — two English names for one column, the unauthored one winning in **every** locale including `en`. The PR declares the label and re-authors the three translations (来源 → 写入组件, ソース → 書き込み元, Origen → Escrito por). The reviewer verified the mechanism on the tree and confirmed it is stated in the changeset body, which ships as CHANGELOG.

### Residuals routed

1. **#19355** — four row-property labels (`report.fields.values`, `report.fields.rows`, `report.fields.dataset`, `dataset.fields.measures`) ship byte-identical to their `en` source in all three locales: 12 leaves of **pre-existing** echo debt on neighbouring panels, ⛔ not this round's and ⛔ not a rider on it. The card carries the reviewer's own caution: an echo is not automatically a defect, so the twelve are judged per leaf, ⛔ never mass-translated.
2. **Prose drift, no card owed.** `metadata-form-zod-reconciliation.test.ts:121` — the `object:fields.options` `subset` row's `why` still says `field.form.ts`'s options repeater 「is schema-derived」; it is now declared and still offers all 6 keys. The sentence is stale, the substance holds, and the next editor of that ledger row is its carrier.
3. **PR body noun, recorded not fixed.** Its sentence 「12 leaves already existed」 should read 12 **keys** (48 leaves); 126 − 14 = 112 is right, the noun is not. ⛔ The body is the dev's artefact and this seat does not rewrite it.
